mainTopic: רבא's question of whether an animal can become a מועד for צרורות, the link to the dispute of רבי טרפון and the חכמים, and the attempts to prove an answer.
overview: The גמרא first rejects an earlier reading of רבי אלעזר and suggests instead that his side and the first תנא argue over whether there is העדאה for צרורות. It then asks why רבא raised this as an open question. The answer is that רבא asks only according to the חכמים who disagree with סומכוס, while both sides of this ברייתא hold like סומכוס. Their real argument is the dispute between רבי טרפון and the חכמים about a תם doing damage in the victim's property. The גמרא shows that רבי טרפון also limits payment to the animal's body, because of דיו, which he accepts whenever it does not cancel the קל וחומר. Next the גמרא returns to רבא's question: is צרורות like קרן, or a sub-type of רגל? Proofs from a hopping chicken and from excrement dropped on dough are each pushed back into the סומכוס and רבנן dispute about a single act. Along the way we learn that excrement counts as צרורות. A new proof begins from a rooster's crow and a horse's neigh that break vessels, and it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Did you ever hear רבי אלעזר say that?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the earlier explanation of רבי אלעזר's opinion. It asks whether he was ever actually heard saying it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did you hear him say that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the explanation it just tried. It points out that רבי אלעזר never said anything like it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier attempt read a split or distinction into רבי אלעזר's ruling about the payment. The גמרא says there is no source showing he held that. So the explanation is dropped, and a new one is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Did you hear him (say so)? This is a way of rejecting an idea that someone never actually said.

phrases.english: Did you hear him [say that]?
phrases.notes: This is a challenge, not a real question. It means: רבי אלעזר never said that, so you can't put those words in his mouth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the explanation of רבי אלעזר given just before this text.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The earlier reading of what רבי אלעזר meant by נזק שלם.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading has no support in anything רבי אלעזר actually said.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר speaks of an animal that was warned
steps.stepSummary: A new explanation: רבי אלעזר's full payment applies when the animal was already warned about kicking pebbles. The argument is whether warning works for צרורות at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבי אלעזר says the owner pays full damages, he means a case where the animal was warned. And this is what they argue about: one holds that warning can apply to pebbles, and the other holds that it cannot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new way to understand רבי אלעזר. His full-damage ruling is about an animal that was already warned (הועד) for kicking pebbles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally pebble damage pays only part of the damage. רבי אלעזר holds that an animal can become מועד for pebbles, and then it pays in full. The תנא קמא holds there is no such thing as warning for pebbles, so it never reaches full payment.

keyTerms.meaning: It was warned. Witnesses testified that the animal kept doing this, so it became a מועד.
The warning or testimony that turns an animal into a מועד.
Pebbles kicked up by an animal as it walks, which then do damage.
They argue about.

phrases.english: Rather, when Rabbi Elazar says
full damages,
it is in a case where it was warned;
and this is what they argue about:
one master holds there is warning for pebbles,
phrases.notes: This first master is רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: and the other master holds there is no warning for pebbles.
phrases.notes: This second master is the תנא קמא, the first opinion in the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the explanation that step 1 rejected.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא): the ruling is about an animal that was warned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אלעזר's full payment rested on a distinction he never stated.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי אלעזר's full payment applies to a warned animal. The dispute is whether warning (העדאה) exists for צרורות.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next step's question about רבא, who asked this very same question as if it were unresolved.

steps.title: Then רבא's question would already be answered
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא contains this dispute, רבא's open question about warning for pebbles is already answered by the תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then what about רבא's question: is there warning for pebbles, or not? According to the חכמים there is none, and according to רבי אלעזר there is!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new explanation. רבא asked whether warning works for pebbles, but this ברייתא would already contain both answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא like רבא would not leave a question open if it were plainly argued in a ברייתא. He would have known each side's answer. So the new reading of the dispute seems to clash with רבא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked. This is used for a real open question or doubt (בעיא).
The חכמים, the majority opinion. Here it is the תנא קמא.

phrases.english: But what about this question that Rava asked:
is there warning for pebbles,
or is there no warning for pebbles?
If according to the Rabbis, there is no warning for pebbles;

phrases.aramaic: אִי לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר – יֵשׁ הַעֲדָאָה לִצְרוֹרוֹת!
phrases.english: if according to Rabbi Elazar, there is warning for pebbles!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 2 that the ברייתא argues over whether there is warning for pebbles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If תנאים already argued this, רבא would not have raised it as an open question.

steps.title: רבא's question follows the חכמים who disagree with סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that his question was only according to the חכמים who disagree with סומכוס. The ברייתא here follows סומכוס, who says pebbles pay full damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא could answer you: when I asked my question, it was according to the חכמים who disagree with סומכוס. But here, both the חכמים and רבי אלעזר hold like סומכוס, who says that for pebbles one pays full damages.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבא's question and the ברייתא's argument belong to two different approaches, so the ברייתא does not answer רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an earlier dispute about the basic payment for pebbles. סומכוס says full damage, and the חכמים say half damage. רבא's question lives inside the view of the חכמים, while both sides of this ברייתא agree with סומכוס. So the ברייתא's argument does not settle רבא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you. This introduces how the person being challenged would answer.
According to the view of.
They hold.

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's question about warning for pebbles stays open. It belongs to the view of the חכמים (half damage), while the ברייתא here follows סומכוס (full damage).
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two disputes. One is the basic payment for pebbles: סומכוס says full, the חכמים say half. The other is whether warning (העדאה) works for pebbles. רבא's question sits inside the half-damage view.

phrases.english: Rava could say to you:
when I myself raise the question,
it is according to the Rabbis
who disagree with Sumakhos;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הָכָא, בֵּין לְרַבָּנַן בֵּין לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר –
phrases.english: but here, both according to the Rabbis and according to Rabbi Elazar,
they hold like Sumakhos,
who says: for pebbles, one pays full damages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the views: the question and the ברייתא follow different underlying opinions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's argument would directly answer רבא's question.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבא asks within the view of the חכמים who disagree with סומכוס. The ברייתא follows סומכוס, so it leaves רבא's question unanswered.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both sides of the ברייתא hold like סומכוס, so the ברייתא is not arguing about העדאה for pebbles after all. The next step explains what they do argue about. רבא's question remains a real open question.

steps.title: Why the חכמים say half damage, and what the real argument is
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of the ברייתא say half damage because the dog did something unusual and was never warned. So the argument between them and רבי אלעזר is really the famous argument between רבי טרפון and the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do the חכמים say half damage? Because the animal acted in an unusual way and was not warned. And they argue about the same thing that רבי טרפון and the חכמים argue about.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its new explanation of the ברייתא. It gives the reason for the half-damage view and links the whole argument to a well-known argument between רבי טרפון and the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The dog's act is treated as unusual behavior (שינוי), like קרן of a תם, so the normal payment is חצי נזק. But the damage happened in the victim's own property. רבי טרפון says a תם that damages in רשות הניזק pays full damage, and the חכמים say half. So רבי אלעזר (full) matches רבי טרפון, and the first תנא (half) matches the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: Half the cost of the damage, the usual payment for a תם
It changed. The animal acted in an unusual way, not its normal behavior
Was warned. The animal was made a מועד through a pattern of repeated damage
A dispute or argument

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes how we read רבי אלעזר. His full-damage ruling is no longer about pebbles at all. It now depends on the larger argument about damage in רשות הניזק.

phrases.aramaic: וְטַעְמָא מַאי אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן חֲצִי נֶזֶק –
phrases.english: And what is the reason the Rabbis said half damage?
Because it acted unusually and was not warned;
and they argue about the same issue that Rabbi Tarfon and the Rabbis argue about.
phrases.notes: That argument is about a תם that does damage in the victim's own property: full damage or half.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַעְמָא מַאי אֲמוּר רַבָּנַן חֲצִי נֶזֶק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the answer and gives a new way to understand the argument in the ברייתא, tying it to רבי טרפון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the dispute. The argument is about a תם in רשות הניזק, not about pebbles.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument between the first תנא and רבי אלעזר was about whether there is העדאה for צרורות (the reading in step 2).
steps.terutzMaskana: The first תנא sees the act as unusual behavior by a תם, so half damage. רבי אלעזר follows רבי טרפון's full damage in רשות הניזק.

steps.title: Does רבי טרפון also say the payment comes only from the animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the link to רבי טרפון. We know he says full damage, but do we know he says the payment comes only from the animal's own body (מגופו), the way רבי אלעזר's ruling has it?
steps.simpleTranslation: Fine, you heard that רבי טרפון says full damage. But did you hear him say it is paid only from the body of the animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the link it just made. The match with רבי טרפון works for the amount, but maybe not for where the money comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's ruling, as presented here, has two parts: full damage, and payment only from the damaging animal itself. רבי טרפון is known for the first part, full damage. The challenge is that nothing we know shows he agrees with the second part, so the two opinions may not truly match.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, grant. "Fine, I'll accept that much"
Full payment for the damage
From its body. Payment is collected only from the damaging animal itself, not from the owner's other property

phrases.aramaic: אֵימוֹר דְּשָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי טַרְפוֹן – נֶזֶק שָׁלֵם;
phrases.english: Say that you heard that according to Rabbi Tarfon it is full damage;
did you hear from him that it is paid from its body?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison between רבי אלעזר and רבי טרפון made in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי אלעזר follows רבי טרפון.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The comparison matches only on full damage. It does not show that רבי טרפון also holds the payment comes only from the animal's body, which is part of רבי אלעזר's ruling.

steps.title: Yes. רבי טרפון learns from קרן, and the rule of דיו limits payment to the animal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes. רבי טרפון learns full damage in רשות הניזק through a קל וחומר from קרן in רשות הרבים. Because of דיו, the result cannot be stricter than its source, and קרן of a תם is paid only from the animal's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. Where does he learn it from? From קרן in רשות הרבים. And it is enough for the thing learned from a קל וחומר to be like the source it was learned from.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the link to רבי טרפון. It shows that the way he learns his rule automatically includes paying only from the animal's body.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי טרפון reasons like this: if a תם goring in רשות הרבים pays half, then in the victim's own property it should surely pay more, so full. But the rule of דיו says a law learned through a קל וחומר cannot go beyond its source. Since goring by a תם in רשות הרבים is paid only from the animal's body, the full payment in רשות הניזק is also paid only from the animal's body.

keyTerms.meaning: Horn. The category of damage done by goring or other unusual, harmful behavior
Public property

keyTerms.term: דַּיּוֹ לַבָּא מִן הַדִּין לִהְיוֹת כַּנִּדּוֹן
keyTerms.meaning: "It is enough for what comes from the reasoning to be like its source." A law learned through a קל וחומר cannot be stricter than the source it came from
Reasoning from a lighter case to a more serious one

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר does match רבי טרפון fully. Full damage comes from the קל וחומר, and the limit to the animal's body comes from דיו.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think דיו cancels רבי טרפון's full payment. In this explanation he still collects full damage. דיו only carries over the limit that payment comes from the animal's body, because that is how the source case works.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule of דיו can carry over the details of a source case, such as where the payment comes from, and not only the amount.

phrases.english: Yes;
from where does he derive it?
phrases.notes: "It" is רבי טרפון's rule that a תם damaging in the victim's property pays full damage.

phrases.english: From Goring in the public domain;
it is enough for what comes from the inference
to be like its source.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6 and confirms that רבי אלעזר follows רבי טרפון.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing the source of the law. The way רבי טרפון learns his rule includes the limit to the animal's body.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון might hold full damage collected from any of the owner's property.
steps.terutzMaskana: Through דיו, רבי טרפון's full payment is also limited to the animal's body, just like his source, קרן in רשות הרבים.

steps.title: Doesn't רבי טרפון reject דיו?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges Step 7. In the משנה, רבי טרפון seems to reject the rule of דיו completely. So how can we say he uses דיו to limit payment to the animal's body?
steps.simpleTranslation: But doesn't רבי טרפון reject the rule of 'דיו'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. We said רבי טרפון uses דיו, but in the משנה he seems to throw דיו out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה about קרן in רשות הניזק, the חכמים answer רבי טרפון with דיו: it should be only half damage, like the source. רבי טרפון does not accept that and says full damage. So it looks as if he never accepts דיו. If so, he could not use דיו to say the payment comes only from the animal's body.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is enough.' A rule that what you learn from a קל וחומר can't be stricter than its source
He does not hold of it / does not accept it

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different things דיו could limit here: the AMOUNT (half or full) and WHERE the money comes from (only the animal's body). רבי טרפון clearly rejects the first. The question is about the second.

phrases.english: But surely רבי טרפון
does not accept 'it is enough'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 7, which used דיו in רבי טרפון's name
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 7's claim that רבי טרפון uses דיו to limit payment to the animal's body
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the משנה, רבי טרפון rejects the חכמים's דיו argument and requires full damage. That shows he does not hold of דיו at all.

steps.title: רבי טרפון rejects דיו only when it would cancel the קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רבי טרפון rejects דיו only when using it would ruin the קל וחומר. When the קל וחומר still teaches something even with דיו, he does accept דיו.
steps.simpleTranslation: When he does not accept 'דיו', that is where it would knock down the קל וחומר. Where it does not knock down the קל וחומר, he does accept 'דיו'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי טרפון does not reject דיו across the board. He rejects it only when it would make the קל וחומר pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole point of his קל וחומר is to add full damage in רשות הניזק. If דיו cut it back to half, the קל וחומר would teach nothing, so there he rejects דיו. But saying the full damage is paid only from the animal's body leaves the קל וחומר alive. So there he accepts דיו, and the link to רבי אלעזר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Is knocked down / refuted
A logical argument from a lighter case to a stricter case
He does hold of it / accepts it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי טרפון uses דיו whenever it does not wipe out the קל וחומר. So he can say full damage, paid only from the animal's body. This confirms that the dispute in the ברייתא matches רבי טרפון and the חכמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear rule for how רבי טרפון uses דיו. It lets the גמרא keep its link between the ברייתא and the famous dispute.

phrases.english: When he does not accept 'it is enough'
that is where the קל וחומר would be knocked down;
phrases.notes: He means: if דיו were applied, the קל וחומר would end up teaching nothing new.

phrases.english: where the קל וחומר is not knocked down
he does accept 'it is enough.'

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי לֵית לֵיהּ ״דַּיּוֹ״ – הֵיכָא דְּמִפְּרִיךְ קַל וָחוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope: רבי טרפון rejects דיו only in one kind of case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי טרפון rejects דיו in every case, so he cannot limit payment to the animal's body.
steps.terutzMaskana: He rejects דיו only where it would cancel the קל וחומר. Where it does not, he accepts it, so the full damage is paid only from the animal's body.

steps.title: Back to רבא's question: can an animal become a מועד for pebbles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to רבא's question itself. Can an animal become a מועד for kicking up pebbles? Is צרורות like קרן, or is it a sub-type of רגל?
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: רבא asked, is there warning for pebbles, or is there no warning for pebbles? Do we compare it to קרן, or perhaps it is a sub-type of רגל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now goes back to רבא's question, which was mentioned earlier, and studies it on its own. This sets up the proofs that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Damage from pebbles is paid at half damage. If צרורות is like קרן, the animal pays half while it is a תם, and full after it is warned and becomes a מועד. If צרורות is a sub-type of רגל, it is normal behavior. Then the half payment is a fixed rule, and warnings change nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself.' The גמרא goes back to study a statement quoted earlier
Warning the owner, which makes the animal a מועד
Pebbles kicked up by an animal as it walks
A sub-type that comes from a main category
Damage an animal does by walking; it is a מועד from the start

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the question of whether pebbles pay half or full. Here we assume half damage. The question is whether warnings can raise it to full.

phrases.english: The matter itself: רבא asked:
phrases.notes: This is the same question of רבא mentioned earlier, in Steps 3-4. Now the גמרא studies it directly.

phrases.english: Is there warning for pebbles,
or is there no warning for pebbles?
Do we compare it to קרן (goring),
or perhaps it is a sub-type of רגל (trampling)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי טרפון discussion and goes back to רבא's question, which was quoted earlier
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether damage from pebbles can go up from half to full payment after the animal is warned three times

steps.title: Proof attempt from a chicken that hops and kicks up pebbles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: for hopping, a chicken is not a מועד, and some say it is. Since plain hopping is normal for a chicken, the ברייתא must mean hopping and kicking up pebbles. This looks like a dispute about warning for pebbles.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: for hopping, it is not a מועד. And some say: it is a מועד. Can you really think this is about plain hopping?! Rather, it means hopping and kicking up pebbles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רבא's question from a ברייתא about a chicken. First it shows that the ברייתא must be talking about pebbles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain hopping is how a chicken normally moves, so nobody would say it is 'not a מועד' for it. So the ברייתא must mean the chicken hopped and kicked up pebbles that did damage. Now the ברייתא's question, 'מועד or not', looks like the same question as רבא's: can there be warning for pebbles?

keyTerms.meaning: Hopping, the way a chicken moves around
An animal treated as warned; its owner pays full damage
Kicked up / sprayed out (pebbles)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
For hopping, it is not a מועד.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא is talking about a chicken.

phrases.english: And some say: it is a מועד.
Can you really think it means plain hopping?!
Rather, it means hopping and kicking up pebbles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer רבא's question from Step 10
steps.raayaObject: רבא's question of whether there is warning for pebbles
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about a chicken hopping, read as hopping and kicking up pebbles, with a dispute over whether it is a מועד

steps.title: Reading the chicken ברייתא as a dispute about warnings for pebbles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא is about a chicken that did this three times. The two opinions would then argue about whether pebbles can ever reach מועד status.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this a case where the chicken did it three times? Then they argue about this: one holds there is העדאה for pebbles, and one holds there is not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the proof from the chicken ברייתא. It says the argument there must be about whether repeated pebble-kicking turns the chicken into a מועד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the chicken kicked pebbles three times, then 'it is a מועד' means העדאה works for צרורות. 'It is not a מועד' means העדאה never works for צרורות. That would answer רבא's question with a dispute between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Being warned three times, which turns an animal into a מועד
Three times
One master holds

phrases.english: What, is it not a case
where it did so three times?
And in this they disagree:
one master holds there is warning,
and one master holds there is no warning?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי, לָאו כְּגוֹן דַּעֲבַד תְּלָתָא זִימְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun in Step 11 by stating which case the ברייתא is about.
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is העדאה for צרורות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about a chicken hopping: 'not a מועד' versus 'some say it is a מועד'

steps.title: No, the chicken did it once, and this is the סומכוס dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes away the proof. Maybe the chicken did it only once, and the argument is the known dispute between סומכוס and רבנן about how much pebble damage costs.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is about one time, and they argue in the dispute of סומכוס and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 12. It offers another way to read the ברייתא that has nothing to do with warnings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס holds that pebble damage is paid in full, and רבנן hold it is paid at half. The two views in the ברייתא may just match these two views about a single act. If so, the ברייתא says nothing about העדאה, and רבא's question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: One time
The Sages, who hold that pebble damage is paid at half

phrases.english: No, it is about one time;
and in the dispute of סומכוס and the Rabbis
they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof in Step 12 by changing the case from three times to one time.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the chicken ברייתא only. רבא's question remains open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as one act, matching the סומכוס/רבנן dispute about payment, not about העדאה.

steps.title: A new proof from an animal that dropped excrement onto dough
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a dispute: רב יהודה says full damage and רבי אלעזר says half damage when an animal drops גללים onto dough. Maybe this is also about three times and העדאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: an animal dropped גללים onto dough. רב יהודה says he pays full damage, and רבי אלעזר says half damage. Isn't it a case where it did so three times, and they argue whether there is העדאה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second source to answer רבא's question. It reads the dispute about dough as an argument over whether העדאה works for pebble-type damage.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Dropped excrement is treated like pebble damage, since it is not direct body contact. If the animal did it three times, רב יהודה would hold it became a מועד and pays full. רבי אלעזר would hold it can never become a מועד for this and always pays half.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal excrement
Dough
Full payment for the damage
Half payment for the damage

phrases.english: Come and hear:
An animal that dropped excrement onto dough,
Rav Yehuda says:
he pays full damage,
and Rabbi Elazar says: half damage.
What, is it not a case
where it did so three times?
And in this they disagree:
one master holds there is warning,
and one master holds there is no warning?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: בְּהֵמָה שֶׁהֵטִילָה גְּלָלִים לְעִיסָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof was pushed away, a new source is brought for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is העדאה for צרורות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רב יהודה and רבי אלעזר about excrement dropped onto dough

steps.title: No, the dough case is also one time and the סומכוס dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes this proof away the same way: maybe it happened once, and רב יהודה and רבי אלעזר simply follow סומכוס and רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It is about one time, and they argue in the dispute of סומכוס and רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof with the same answer it used in Step 13.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה, who says full, would follow סומכוס. רבי אלעזר, who says half, would follow רבנן. With this reading the dispute is about a single act, so it still does not answer רבא's question.

phrases.english: No; it is about one time,
and in the dispute of סומכוס and the Rabbis
they disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 14 in the same way Step 13 rejected Step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the dough case only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The dispute can be about one act, matching the סומכוס/רבנן dispute over payment for pebbles.

steps.title: But dropping excrement onto dough is unusual behavior
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the new reading. Dropping excrement onto dough is unusual, and unusual behavior falls under קרן, which pays only half. So how can רב יהודה say full damage?
steps.simpleTranslation: But this is unusual behavior!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the one-time reading from Step 15. If the act is unusual, no one should say full damage for a first time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pebble damage can be full only according to סומכוס, and only when it comes from normal behavior, like רגל. Unusual behavior is a kind of קרן, where a תם pays only half. That would leave רב יהודה's full-damage ruling without a basis.

keyTerms.meaning: Unusual, out of character, which is treated like קרן

phrases.english: But it is unusual!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the one-time reading given in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב יהודה's full damage for a single act follows סומכוס
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An unusual act is like קרן and pays half the first time, so full damage cannot be explained by סומכוס.

steps.title: The animal was squeezed in and had no choice
steps.stepSummary: The animal was pressed into a tight spot and had nowhere else to relieve itself, so the act is not unusual.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where the area was crowded and squeezed it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by setting up the case so that the behavior counts as normal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal was forced into a tight space with no other option, dropping excrement on the dough is natural, not strange. So it is not קרן, and סומכוס's rule of full payment for pebbles can apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressed, squeezed in
Literally 'the world,' here meaning the crowd or surroundings

phrases.english: Where the surroundings squeezed it in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Dropping excrement on dough is unusual, so it falls under קרן.
steps.terutzMaskana: The animal was forced into it, so the act is normal and can follow the pebble rules.

steps.title: Then why not simply say 'the הלכה follows סומכוס'?
steps.stepSummary: If רב יהודה and רבי אלעזר only repeat the סומכוס/רבנן dispute, they should have just said 'the הלכה follows סומכוס' or 'the הלכה follows רבנן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Let רב יהודה say: the הלכה is like סומכוס. And let רבי אלעזר say: the הלכה is like רבנן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the אמוראים only repeat an old dispute. Why would they say it through a new case?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא who agrees with one side of a תנאים dispute normally just says 'the הלכה follows so-and-so.' Bringing a whole new case suggests they are teaching something new, perhaps about העדאה.

keyTerms.meaning: The final law follows (this opinion)
Then let him say

phrases.english: But let Rav Yehuda say:
the halakha is like סומכוס,
and let Rabbi Elazar say:
the halakha is like the Rabbis!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to the one-time reading, this time attacking the way the אמוראים worded their dispute.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the dough dispute simply repeats the סומכוס/רבנן dispute
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If nothing new were taught, they would have just ruled 'הלכה כ...' instead of stating a new case.

steps.title: The new case teaches that excrement counts as pebbles
steps.stepSummary: The אמוראים needed the case of גללים. We might have thought excrement is like the animal's body, since it comes from the body. They teach that it is treated like pebbles.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of excrement was needed. You might have thought that since it is pulled along after the body, it is like the body itself. So they teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge: the new case teaches a new point, so the one-time reading stands.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this case, one could think excrement is like direct body damage (רגל), which always pays full, with no dispute. By arguing over it in the סומכוס/רבנן terms, the אמוראים show it counts as צרורות. So the dispute is still about payment, not העדאה, and רבא's question stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed for him
You might have thought to say
Pulled along, drawn after
He teaches us (otherwise)

steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs about העדאה for צרורות were pushed back into the סומכוס/רבנן dispute about a single act. Along the way we learn that dropped excrement is treated as צרורות, not as the animal's body.

phrases.english: Excrement was needed for him;
it would enter your mind to say,
since they are drawn after its body,
they are like its body;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18 by showing what new point the dough case teaches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying a new point (חידוש) that justifies the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Excrement comes from the body, so it counts as the body itself and always pays in full.
steps.terutzMaskana: Excrement counts as צרורות, so the סומכוס/רבנן dispute applies to it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the category of excrement damage as צרורות and keeps רבא's question about העדאה still open.

steps.title: A rooster's crow and a horse's neigh that break vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings two teachings about damage done by sound. In the rooster case the owner pays full damage, and in the horse and donkey case he pays half.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רמי בר יחזקאל taught that if a rooster stuck its head into a glass vessel, crowed, and broke it, the owner pays full damage. And רב יוסף said that בי רב say: if a horse neighed or a donkey brayed and broke vessels, the owner pays half damage.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two sources to start a new proof about whether צרורות can become מועד. This step only sets up the sources. The actual argument comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Breaking something with sound is damage by the animal's force, not its body, so it works like צרורות. Yet one source says full damage and the other says half. The גמרא will treat this as a dispute and try to use it to answer רבא's question.

keyTerms.meaning: Rooster
Glass vessel
Neighed (a horse's sound)
Brayed (a donkey's sound)
The school of רב, his students

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is about to read these two sources as a real dispute about the same situation. It will suggest that both are about an animal that did this three times, and that they argue over whether העדאה works for צרורות. The same pattern was used for the chicken and the dough.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל:
phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rami bar Yeḥezkel taught:
A rooster that stuck out its head
into the inside space of a glass vessel,
and crowed into it and broke it –
pays full damage.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמְרִי בֵּי רַב:
phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said, the school of Rav say:
A horse that neighed and a donkey that brayed,
and broke the vessels –
pays half damage.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּתָנֵי רָמֵי בַּר יְחֶזְקֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the earlier proof was pushed away and its follow-up questions were settled, the גמרא tries a new source for the same question.
steps.raayaObject: Whether צרורות can become מועד and pay full damage
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רמי בר יחזקאל (rooster, full damage) together with the teaching of בי רב (horse and donkey, half damage)

steps.title: Suggesting both sources speak of three times and argue over העדאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that both sources are about an animal that did this three times. Then the full-damage view would hold that there is העדאה for צרורות, and the half-damage view would hold that there is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What, is it not a case where it did it three times?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that the two sources are about an animal that had already done this three times, so they would be arguing about whether העדאה works for צרורות. The sentence is not finished here and continues right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sound damage works like צרורות. If both cases are about an animal that did this three times, then רמי בר יחזקאל, who says full damage, holds that העדאה works for צרורות. בי רב, who say half damage, hold that it does not. That would show רבא's question is a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: What, is it not...? The גמרא suggests the obvious reading as a proof
Three times; the number that makes an animal מועד
An animal with a proven habit of damaging, whose owner pays full damage

steps.whyThisMatters: If this proof holds, רבא's question would turn out to be a known dispute, with one side saying there is העדאה for צרורות and the other saying there is not.

phrases.english: What, is it not in a case
where it did it three times –
phrases.notes: He means the animals in both sources. The גמרא's sentence keeps going after this.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי, לָאו כְּגוֹן דַּעֲבַד תְּלָתָא זִימְנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the two sources from step 20 and starts to read them as a dispute about whether there is העדאה for צרורות after three times.
steps.raayaObject: Whether there is העדאה for צרורות
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רמי בר יחזקאל (full payment) and בי רב (half payment), read as both being about an animal that did this three times
